sources.license: Terrain data: open-data sources listed at https://mapterhorn.com/attribution (USGS 3DEP public domain; Copernicus GLO-30 free and open licence)
sources.upstream: Mapterhorn build from USGS 3DEP 1 m where available, USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second and Copernicus GLO-30 (per-tile source not stated)

steps: OSM ways with piste:type, ski/ski:nordic/snowshoe access tags, or membership in route=piste/ski relations (relation piste tags fill ways that lack their own).
Tag rules in classify.py assign ski_descent, ascent_skin, approach or touring_area; every feature carries classBasis. Ways without a winter or ski tag are never included.

Candidates inside lift-served context (within 500 m of an operating downhill ski-area polygon, 3 km of an operating or proposed ski-area point without polygon, or 1 km of a lift) are excluded and counted; abandoned ski areas do not count as lift-served.
USFS TrailNFS segments with nonmotorized winter use (snowshoe or cross-country ski allowed or managed) added as approach.
Geometry simplified with Douglas-Peucker (ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology) at the configured tolerance; coordinates rounded.

lengthM is the geodesic length of the unsimplified source geometry. dem* fields sample the Mapterhorn DEM (z13) along the unsimplified line at 7.5 m spacing; aspect is degrees clockwise from true north (Web Mercator grid north is true north).
OpenSkiData runs were used only as a cross-check of OSM ski-touring counts (same OSM origin, unstable ids); they are not duplicated here.

units.demMinElevM: metres (Mapterhorn; NAVD88 where the source is USGS 3DEP)
units.demMeanAspectDeg: degrees clockwise from true north, downslope direction
units.demAspectResultant: 0..1 circular resultant length (1 = all samples share one aspect)

limitations: OSM tags do not say whether a ski-touring way is the up track or the descent. ascent_skin is the default for undirected tour routes; ski_descent is used for downhill pistes outside lift-served context and for tour ways whose source name names a descent feature (couloir, face, chute, bowl, gully, glade). See classBasis.
approach means a source tag records winter or ski use on that way. It does not mean the route is open, plowed, signed, legal to park at, or safe.
Route presence or absence says nothing about avalanche hazard. DEM metrics describe terrain shape only.
Coverage is sparse and uneven; see docs/coverage-routes.md. Absence of a line is not absence of a route.

DEM metrics come from Mapterhorn z13 tiles (512 px, about 7.4 m pixels at 39 N), built from USGS 3DEP 1 m where available, 3DEP 1/3 arc-second and Copernicus GLO-30; which source fills a given tile is not stated. docs/sources/map-routes.md section 5.5 measured Mapterhorn minus current 3DEP RMSE 1.4 to 1.9 m near Berthoud Pass. Gain and loss are raw sums of sampled steps without smoothing, so they include DEM noise; short lines and sharp features are smoothed by bilinear sampling.

dem.name: Mapterhorn terrain tiles (Terrarium-encoded WebP, 512 px), zoom 13
dem.upstream: Mapterhorn build from USGS 3DEP 1 m where available, USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second and Copernicus GLO-30 (per-tile source not stated)
dem.accuracy: docs/sources/map-routes.md section 5.5: Mapterhorn minus current 3DEP RMSE 1.4 to 1.9 m near Berthoud Pass
dem.aspectMethod: Horn 3x3 on the Web Mercator tile grid with per-latitude pixel size; degrees clockwise from true north
